principles: Review freshness and closeout artifact admissibility are separate decisions; retaining review never authenticates an artifact.
Canonical or registered closeout metadata may move HEAD but cannot weaken review of unchanged materialHash, storyFilesHash, scope, policy, command set, or review round.
Scope-defining metadata, unknown writers, malformed lineage, manual tampering, and any real material drift remain fail-closed.
drivers: Eliminate repeated metadata-only review rounds in unattended workflows.
Preserve fail-closed artifact and assurance semantics.
Keep phase admission, dispatch, gate consumers, and process facts mechanically aligned.

options.name: A: separate review retention from artifact admissibility, then align closeout ordering
pros: Preserves code-review freshness without granting metadata PASS authority
Keeps each closeout artifact independently checked at its consuming gate
Supports a measurable one-pass lifecycle regression
cons: Touches review freshness and several lifecycle consumers
Needs explicit negative matrices to prevent accidental trust expansion

options.name: B: authenticate same-UID closeout receipts and reuse them as authority
cons: Same local UID cannot prove canonical writer authority
Would weaken the existing security boundary
Conflates causal audit evidence with artifact admissibility

options.name: C: reorder commands or whitelist paths at each gate
cons: Does not remove the class of metadata invalidation
Duplicates policy and can miss future writers

chosen: A: separate review retention from artifact admissibility, then align closeout ordering
rationale: Choose A because the observed loop is a freshness-coupling defect, not proof that local closeout receipts are authoritative. Review receipts may remain fresh only when reviewed material, story-owned files, scope, policy, command set, and review round are unchanged and every intervening path is registered nonmaterial closeout metadata. This retention result must never mark the changed artifact admissible; test evidence, DONE-required evidence, delivery checks, summaries, and transcripts remain independently fail-closed at their own gates.

preMortem.scenario: A forged or manually edited closeout file inherits authority
preMortem.trigger: A review-retention result is reused as artifact admissibility
preMortem.consequence: Untrusted closeout evidence can satisfy TEST or DONE
preMortem.mitigation: Expose separate retention and admissibility results; assert retention cannot satisfy artifact gates and add malformed, unsigned, unknown-writer, and tamper negatives.

preMortem.trigger: Retention ignores materialHash, storyFilesHash, scope, policy, command set, config, or review round
preMortem.consequence: Changed behavior inherits old review PASS
preMortem.mitigation: Fail closed on every identity mismatch and cover the full source/story-owned/config/policy/command-set matrix.

preMortem.trigger: Dispatch and mutation policies admit different phases or closeout writes happen after the last binding point
preMortem.consequence: Normal closeout requires another review round
preMortem.mitigation: Align delivery dispatch/write phases and prove a complete REVIEW to TEST to DONE transcript with zero metadata rollback, re-attestation, human confirmation, and unchanged-suite execution.

preMortem.scenario: Concept gate stops detecting true deletions
preMortem.trigger: Body-edit false-positive filtering is broader than declaration-aware deletion detection
preMortem.consequence: Removed declarations with residual references pass
preMortem.mitigation: Test body edit, signature edit, overload, rename, true deletion, and residual-reference cases separately.
